plan_title: Oxy Seminole San Andres Unit Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The Seminole San Andres Unit boundary plus a half-mile buffer, projected to contain the free-phase plume through the project and five years after injection (p16-17).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA; the stabilized plume is projected to stay inside the unit (p18).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores and surface equipment are treated as the only meaningful pathways; faults (Devonian faults tip out about 1,700 ft below the zone), seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated low or no risk (p8, p19-23).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. Existing automated operational data (injection set points from ongoing reservoir modeling, production forecasts, inspection work orders, H2S alarms) are used to flag excursions (p29-30).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31, with the mass balance and leakage estimates; equipment leaks reported under Subpart W; records kept at least three years; the discontinuation request is to include two to three or more years of post-injection data. No commitment to publish data or report to the state UIC program (p24, p29-30, p34, p36-37).

rows.detail: Custody transfer meter M2 on pipeline CO2 and meter M3 on recycled CO2 from the gas plant; flow measured continually, injected CO2 sampled at least quarterly, received-CO2 concentration taken from the sales contract.
rows.location: Custody transfer point (M2) and Seminole Gas Processing Plant outlet (M3)
rows.evidence_quote: This meter measures flow rate continually.

rows.detail: Injection pressure monitored continually against pattern plans programmed into WAG skids; automatic flags on deviations and automatic shutoff on overpressure; SCADA monitors wellhead pressure.
rows.location: Each injection well and WAG skid
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressure or rate outside set points: automatic flag, field investigation, work order; WAG skids shut off if pressure exceeds programmed settings.
rows.evidence_quote: Pressure in injection wells is monitored on a continual basis.

rows.detail: Annular pressure in wellheads monitored to detect tubing and casing leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly: inspect and repair; if extensive, well shut in, work order, leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: monitoring of the annular pressure in wellheads

rows.detail: MITs on injectors listed in the response plan as the check for tubing and casing leaks; no testing interval or rule citation given.
rows.trigger_or_response: Tubing or casing leak: wellbore shut in, workover crews respond within days.
rows.evidence_quote: Monitor changes in tubing and annulus pressure; Mechanical Integrity Testing (MIT) for injectors

rows.detail: Each producer tested about once every two months through satellite test stations (8-12 hours); produced gas sampled at least quarterly for CO2; results compared with model forecast.
rows.location: Each production well; satellite test stations; gas plant meter
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant deviation from forecast: well management personnel investigate; work order if unresolved.
rows.evidence_quote: each well being tested approximately once every two months

rows.detail: Reservoir pressure collected for modeling and operations and routinely updated with FPP (step-rate tests); read at WAG skids and in new wells; past interference tests cited. No observation wells or gauges named.
rows.location: Injection zone, via WAG skids and new wells
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexplained pressure changes: investigate; reseal abandoned wells, manage lease-line fluids, or shut in injectors and assess the reservoir.
rows.evidence_quote: The reservoir pressure in the SSAU is collected for use in reservoir modeling and operations management.

rows.detail: Routine field inspections of wells and surface facilities for white CO2 clouds and ice; also used to spot unapproved drilling.
rows.trigger_or_response: Problem found: investigate, work order tracked to completion, leak quantified.
rows.evidence_quote: Field inspections are conducted on a routine basis by field personnel.

rows.detail: All field personnel wear H2S monitors (alarm at 10 ppm); injected gas is about 1% H2S, so H2S serves as a proxy for CO2 leaks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Alarm: protect personnel, investigate source, quantify CO2 leak for the annual report.
rows.evidence_quote: H2S monitors are worn by all field personnel.

rows.detail: Profile logs, micro-resistivity imaging and existing open- and cased-hole logs were used for site characterization (fault screening, geomodel); no logging is run as monitoring.
rows.evidence_quote: downhole measurements from profile logs and micro‐resistivity imaging tools show no indication of conductive faults or fractures

rows.detail: Oxy participates in the public TexNet network and says it will keep monitoring for seismic signals; a December 2022 USGS review (M3.0+) found none near the unit, nearest about 30 miles away. No site array.
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismic event: shut in nearby injectors, assess the reservoir, corrective action as needed.
rows.evidence_quote: will continue to monitor for seismic signals that could indicate the creation of potential leakage pathways in SSAU

rows.detail: Seismic data acquired over the unit were analyzed (including coherence attributes) to map Devonian faults and rule out leakage pathways; no repeat seismic.
rows.evidence_quote: Oxy extensively analyzed seismic data acquired over the SSAU to assess potential leakage pathways and basement‐rooted faults.

rows.detail: Subpart W emission factors and engineering estimates used to quantify surface equipment leaks and vents, reconciled with event-driven estimates to avoid double counting.
rows.evidence_quote: In accordance with §98.444(d), Oxy uses 40 CFR §98 Subpart W to estimate the mass of CO2 emitted from equipment leaks at the SSAU.

rows.detail: Pipeline leak detection: personnel monitor the pipeline continuously through SCADA.
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak detected: mitigate and quantify under Subpart W.
rows.evidence_quote: Personnel continuously monitor the pipeline using the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system and can detect and mitigate pipeline leaks expeditiously.

rows.detail: History-matched tNavigator reservoir model used to track injected CO2, forecast production, and set injector targets through ongoing modeling; predictive modeling plus monitoring data to support discontinuation.
rows.evidence_quote: Track injected CO2, identify how and where CO2 is trapped in the SSAU, and monitor sequestration mass and distribution.

notes: Same Oxy template as West Seminole and South Plains. Reporter number is a placeholder ('XXXX', p4). Received-CO2 concentration is said to come from the sales contract (p26) and also from the gas measurement database (p31). Meter labels conflict: M4 is the produced-gas meter (p26) and also the oil-sales meter (p33), and produced gas flow is said to be measured at the SGPP outlet (p35). The appendix well list is dated September 2020 though the well counts are November 2022 (p12, p38). Producers are tested about every two months (no bimonthly value in the vocabulary; coded periodic_unspecified). Profile logs, image logs and seismic were used for fault characterization only (coded mentioned_only). Figures are images.
